## 2. FluidAudio (Parakeet TDT CoreML)

- **Package**: `https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio.git`. **Latest v0.17.7 (2026-10-08)**; README still says `from: "0.12.4"`; swiftpackageregistry is stale at 0.15.6 ([releases](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/releases)). Package.swift: **iOS 17+**, macOS 14+, visionOS 2+, swift-tools 6.0, no external deps ([Package.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Package.swift)).
- **Models** (`AsrModelVersion`): `.v2` (EN, LibriSpeech test-clean WER 2.1%), `.v3` (25 EU langs, 2.27–2.5%, "~480 MB"), `.ultra` (2.13%, int8 encoder 595 MB, iOS 17+, total ≈ 632 MB per HF tree), `.redux` (2-bit encoder 183 MB, **~220 MB download**, 2.71% WER, **iOS 18+**), `.phonon2` (fastest v3-family on ANE, 2.47%, iOS 18+) ([v0.17.3 notes](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/releases), [benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). v3 files: `Encoder.mlmodelc` 445 MB + Decoder 24 + JointDecision 13 + Preprocessor 0.5 + `parakeet_vocab.json` ≈ 483 MB (HF tree API, `FluidInference/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml`).
- **Speed**: 155–210x RTFx on M4 Pro; **no published iPhone RTFx**. iPhone 16 Pro Max encoder compile: 3.36 s cold / 0.16 s warm; iPhone 13: 4.40 s cold ([benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). RN wrapper README: ~500 MB total, first init 20–30 s, later ~1 s ([react-native-fluidaudio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/react-native-fluidaudio/main/README.md)). Independent 3rd-party estimate ~47x on iPhone 15 Pro (extrapolated, not measured) ([TowardsAI](https://pub.towardsai.net/parakeet-vs-whisper-for-local-dictation-speed-accuracy-and-vocabulary-in-2026-f809fcc4271c)).
- **Timestamps**: `ASRResult{text, confidence, duration, processingTime, tokenTimings:[TokenTiming]?}`; `TokenTiming{token, tokenId, startTime, endTime, confidence}` are **subword tokens**; free function `public func buildWordTimings(from:) -> [WordTiming{word,startTime,endTime}]` merges on `▁` boundaries ([AsrTypes.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Sources/FluidAudio/ASR/Parakeet/AsrTypes.swift)).

let asr = AsrManager(config: .default); try await asr.loadModels(models)

- **Models** (`AsrModelVersion`): `.v2` (EN, LibriSpeech test-clean WER 2.1%), `.v3` (25 EU langs, 2.27–2.5%, "~480 MB"), `.ultra` (2.13%, int8 encoder 595 MB, iOS 17+, total ≈ 632 MB per HF tree), `.redux` (2-bit encoder 183 MB, **~220 MB download**, 2.71% WER, **iOS 18+**), `.phonon2` (fastest v3-family on ANE, 2.47%, iOS 18+) ([v0.17.3 notes](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/releases), [benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). v3 files: `Encoder.mlmodelc` 445 MB + Decoder 24 + JointDecision 13 + Preprocessor 0.5 + `parakeet_vocab.json` ≈ 483 MB (HF tree API, `FluidInference/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml`).
- **Speed**: 155–210x RTFx on M4 Pro; **no published iPhone RTFx**. iPhone 16 Pro Max encoder compile: 3.36 s cold / 0.16 s warm; iPhone 13: 4.40 s cold ([benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). RN wrapper README: ~500 MB total, first init 20–30 s, later ~1 s ([react-native-fluidaudio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/react-native-fluidaudio/main/README.md)). Independent 3rd-party estimate ~47x on iPhone 15 Pro (extrapolated, not measured) ([TowardsAI](https://pub.towardsai.net/parakeet-vs-whisper-for-local-dictation-speed-accuracy-and-vocabulary-in-2026-f809fcc4271c)).
- **Timestamps**: `ASRResult{text, confidence, duration, processingTime, tokenTimings:[TokenTiming]?}`; `TokenTiming{token, tokenId, startTime, endTime, confidence}` are **subword tokens**; free function `public func buildWordTimings(from:) -> [WordTiming{word,startTime,endTime}]` merges on `▁` boundaries ([AsrTypes.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Sources/FluidAudio/ASR/Parakeet/AsrTypes.swift)).

let dir = Bundle.main.resourceURL!.appendingPathComponent("parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml")

let asr = AsrManager(config: .default); try await asr.loadModels(models)
let r = try await asr.transcribe(samples16kMono, source: .system)   // or transcribe(fileURL, source: .system)
let words = buildWordTimings(from: r.tokenTimings ?? [])             // [WordTiming(word,startTime,endTime)]
```

- Upstream **v1.13.8 (2026-09-10)**; tagged release has **no iOS asset** (build with `build-ios.sh`). - Timestamps: every offline result exposes `tokens`, `timestamps:[Float]`, `durations`; Whisper adds `enableTokenTimestamps`/`enableSegmentTimestamps` and `segmentTimestamps/segmentTexts` ([SherpaOnnx.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/master/swift-api-examples/SherpaOnnx.swift)). Models: Whisper, Zipformer, Parakeet TDT v2/v3, SenseVoice, Moonshine, Dolphin, Paraformer.
- Sizes: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 int8 ≈ 640 MB ([docs](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/pretrained_models/offline-transducer/nemo-transducer-models.html)); whisper tiny.en int8 ≈ 117 MB (decoder 105 MB) ([docs](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/pretrained_models/whisper/tiny.en.html)).

## 4. whisper.cpp

- **v1.9.5 (2026-10-06)**: tagged releases ship **source only**; only nightly builds attach `whisper-bNNNN-xcframework.zip` (b5454, 62.8 MB) ([releases API](https://api.github.com/repos/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/releases?per_page=30)). SPM = `binaryTarget(url: ...xcframework.zip, checksum:)`.
- CoreML encoder: must run `generate-coreml-model.sh` yourself (Python/coremltools), ">3x faster" encoder, first run slow ([README](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp)). ggml sizes: tiny 75 MiB, base 142, small 466; q5 ≈ 40% of that.
- Word timestamps: C `whisper_full_params.token_timestamps` + experimental `dtw_token_timestamps` with `dtw_aheads_preset` ([whisper.h](https://fr.github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/blob/master/whisper.h)). `exPHAT/SwiftWhisper` is **1.2.0 from 2023-08**, segments only — stale.
- Verdict: most glue, no ANE decoder, worse WER/size than Parakeet. Skip for 6 h.

## 5. Newer options (2026)

- **Moonshine Voice** (2026-02-13, MIT): `https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine-swift`, iOS 14+, CPU-only; tiny 26 MB … medium-streaming 245 MB at **6.65% OpenASR WER** (Whisper large-v3: 7.44%), iPhone 12 latency 25–90 ms ([blog](https://petewarden.com/2026/02/13/announcing-moonshine-voice/), [iOS guide](https://mintlify.wiki/moonshine-ai/moonshine/platforms/ios)). Swift API gives **line-level** `TranscriptLine{startTime,duration}` only, no word timings ([data structures](https://mintlify.wiki/moonshine-ai/moonshine/api/swift/data-structures)). Great size/speed, weak for diarization merge.
- **Kyutai STT** (word timestamps, CC-BY-4.0 weights): runs via MLX in `moshi-swift`, "1b model tested on iPhone 16 Pro" ([DSM repo](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/delayed-streams-modeling)); MLX-Swift build + ~GB weights = not a 6-hour job.
- **speech-swift** (`soniqo/speech-swift`): iOS 18+, `branch: "main"` only; Parakeet CoreML "32x real-time" (device unspecified, **no word timestamps** on Parakeet), Qwen3-ASR, Omnilingual (0.28 RTF iPhone 16 Pro), Voxtral Mini 3B (MLX, Mac-class) ([repo](https://github.com/soniqo/speech-swift)).
- **Argmax Pro SDK 3** (2026-09-23) adds Parakeet etc. but is proprietary → excluded. FluidAudio 0.15.6+ also has a Canary-1B-v2 engine (heavier, no iPhone numbers).

## Ranked recommendation

1. **FluidAudio Parakeet** — `.v2` if English-only (2.1% WER, 480 MB), `.v3` multilingual, `.redux` if the 220 MB footprint wins the size score (iOS 18+). Bundle the folder, `buildWordTimings`, use its `DiarizerManager`. ~30 lines of glue.
2. **WhisperKit base.en (145 MB) or 626 MB large-v3-turbo** — if you need iOS 16, want word probabilities, or hit a FluidAudio ANE crash on the judge's iOS build. Also has SpeakerKit for diarization.
3. sherpa-onnx (only for exotic models), 4. Moonshine (size/speed demo, no words), 5. whisper.cpp (skip).

Note on caveats: neither FluidAudio nor Argmax publish iPhone peak-memory numbers; the only hard iPhone data are Argmax's speed factors and FluidAudio's compile times above.</result>

**Where the code lives now.** `MLXLLM`/`MLXLMCommon` moved out of `mlx-swift-examples` into **`ml-explore/mlx-swift-lm`** (examples repo keeps only the apps). **Simulator: NO.** MLX issue #2605: "MLX does not run on iOS simulators… you get a mysterious crash"; maintainer (awni) chose to block it rather than add a CPU path (closed Mar 2026). Debug on a Mac target or device only. ([mlx#2605](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/issues/2605), [strathweb](https://strathweb.com/2025/03/running-phi-models-on-ios-with-apple-mlx-framework/))

**Bundled model → stream with chat template (3.x API, ~15 lines).** Add the HF snapshot folder to Xcode as a *folder reference* (blue), uncompressed:

Memory.cacheLimit = 20 * 1024 * 1024          // LLMEval does this; was MLX.GPU.set(cacheLimit:)
let dir = Bundle.main.url(forResource: "Qwen3-1.7B-4bit", withExtension: nil)!
let model = try await loadModelContainer(from: dir, using: #huggingFaceTokenizerLoader()) // no Hub, no network

    generateParameters: GenerateParameters(maxTokens: 700, temperature: 0.3),
    additionalContext: ["enable_thinking": false])   // "values provided for the chat template rendering context" → Qwen3 no-think

Signatures verified in `ModelFactory.swift` (`loadModelContainer(from directory: URL, using: any TokenizerLoader)`), `ModelConfiguration(directory:)`, `ChatSession.init(_:instructions:…additionalContext:…)`, `streamResponse(to:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<String,Error>`. Belt-and-braces for Qwen3: also append `/no_think` and strip `<think>…</think>`.

**Memory.** Add entitlement `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit = true` (LLMEval README). Per-app ceiling is **~6 GB even on 12 GB iPhone 17 Pro Max** with the entitlement ([Apple forum, Jun 2026](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/834805)). A ≤1 GB model + ≤1 GB KV fits 6 GB-RAM phones (iPhone 15) if you keep `cacheLimit` small. Gotcha: MLX's reported peak RSS is far higher than llama.cpp's for the same model (Llama-3.2-3B: 2,508 MB vs 696 MB mmap'd; Gemma-4-E2B: 3,010 vs 191 MB) — judges measuring memory will notice. `Memory.activeMemory/peakMemory/clearCache()` exist for stats.

Latest **b11493 (2026-10-08), 60.07 MB zip** (llama.cpp also tags `v0.6.0`, but the xcframework is on the b-tags). Add as `binaryTarget(name: "llama", url: ".../releases/download/b11493/llama-b11493-xcframework.zip", checksum: …)` — **zero compile time**.

Raw C API: `llama_model_default_params()` → `n_gpu_layers = 99`; `llama_model_load_from_file`; `llama_init_from_model` with `n_ctx`, `n_batch`, `flash_attn_type`, `type_k/type_v = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0` (halves KV); template: `llama_model_chat_template(model, nil)` + `llama_chat_apply_template(tmpl, msgs, n, true, buf, len)`.

The JSON-schema→GBNF converter is C++ `common/`, not in the xcframework — hand-write ~5 GBNF rules (`root ::= "{" ws "\"summary\":" ws string "," ws "\"decisions\":" ws arr "," ws "\"action_items\":" ws arr "}"`) or pre-generate with `json_schema_to_grammar.py`.

## 5. Prompting & long transcripts

- **Single pass, 8k ctx**: 1k–6k tokens fits every candidate. Prefill on 17 Pro ≈ 1–3k tok/s (2–6 s for 6k); ~2–3× slower on 15 Pro. KV budget: Qwen3-1.7B 8k ≈ 0.9 GB fp16 (set `kvBits: 8` / `type_k=q8_0`), LFM2.5/Qwen3.5 ≈ 0.1 GB. Only map-reduce if >8k tokens or 6 GB phones: chunk ~2k tokens on speaker turns, 100-token overlap, extract per chunk, one merge pass that dedupes decisions/actions.
- Pre-clean the transcript (drop timestamps, fillers) — 20–40% fewer tokens, free speed.
- **Markdown with fixed headings** (`## Summary`, `## Decisions`, `## Action Items` as `- [Owner] task — due`) is the most reliable free-form format for 1–2B models; JSON only when grammar-enforced (llama.cpp GBNF, or `MLXGuidedGeneration` JSON-Schema/EBNF — `GrammarConstraint(tokenizer:jsonSchema:…)` + `GuidedGenerationLoop.run`, iOS 17+, pre-warm off the main actor since grammar compile blocks hundreds of ms). Otherwise lenient-parse + one retry.
- System prompt <150 tokens: "Use only facts in the transcript; write 'None' if no decisions; max 5 bullets per section." Skip few-shot (prefill cost > gain). temperature 0.2–0.4, top_p 0.9, repetition_penalty 1.05–1.1, maxTokens 600–800, thinking disabled.

## Recommendation (6-hour build)

1. **MLX Swift (`mlx-swift-lm` 3.32.3) + `mlx-community/Qwen3-1.7B-4bit`** (985 MB, Apache-2.0, `enable_thinking:false`, `kvBits: 8`). Best-documented iOS path, ~40 tok/s on 17 Pro / ~30 on 15–16 Pro, ChatSession streaming in 15 lines, strict open-source. If the license bar is "open-weight", swap the folder for **`LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-MLX-4bit`** (659 MB, 60 tok/s, best IFEval) — zero code change. Try **Qwen3.5-2B text-only (1.06 GB)** last, only if time remains (long-context win, but unbenchmarked on iPhone MLX and a third-party conversion).
2. **Fallback: llama.cpp `b11493` xcframework (or LLM.swift) + Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M (1.11 GB) / LFM2.5 Q4_K_M (731 MB) + GBNF for guaranteed JSON.** No compile time, runs in the simulator (CPU), lowest RSS, ~20–25% slower decode than MLX.

Gotchas to say out loud: device-only testing for MLX; add the memory entitlement; bundle as folder reference (not compressed asset); strip `<think>`; warm up once before timing; expect thermal decay after ~2 min.

No published number; budget **~5–10 min first build** on an M-series Mac and start it immediately. Binary adds the static lib + `mlx.metallib` (tens of MB; mlx#163 flags it as "too large" concern).

**Measured tok/s (MLX Swift).**
- iPhone 17 Pro, 4-bit, iOS 26.3, medium prompt ([Feb 2026](https://rickytakkar.com/blog_russet_mlx_benchmark.html)): Qwen3-0.6B **62.2**, LFM2.5-1.2B **59.7**, Llama-3.2-1B **58.1**, Qwen3-1.7B **39.5**, Gemma-3-1B-QAT **37.1**. TTFT@47 tok: LFM2.5 244 ms, Qwen3-1.7B 360 ms; Gemma-3-1B prefill is slow (1,330 ms @ 690 tok). Decode drops up to 38% at long contexts.
- iPhone 17 Pro ([john-rocky harness](https://github.com/john-rocky/apple-silicon-llm-bench)): Qwen3-0.6B MLX 178.8 tok/s; Gemma-4-E2B MLX-Swift 49.1 tok/s decode, 3,274 tok/s prefill @1024; **sustained 10 min: MLX falls to ~18 tok/s (38% retained)** — thermal throttling is real; warm up before demos and don't loop generation.
- iPhone 16 Pro, Q4 ([May 2026](https://www.buildmvpfast.com/blog/on-device-llm-mobile-llama-ios-android-2026)): Llama-3.2-1B 52 tok/s, 3B 23 tok/s; –44% after ~2 min.
- iPhone Air (A19 = iPhone 17 class, [Sep 2026](https://ananasdda.github.io/pocket-ai-lab/benchmarks/)): Gemma-2-2B MLX 37.9, Qwen2.5-3B MLX 30.8.

## 2. llama.cpp route (fallback)

- **`Package.swift` was removed from llama.cpp** (2025). Every `bNNNNN` release ships `llama-bNNNNN-xcframework.zip` (device + simulator + macOS/visionOS/tvOS, Metal on). Latest **b11493 (2026-10-08), 60.07 MB zip** (llama.cpp also tags `v0.6.0`, but the xcframework is on the b-tags). Add as `binaryTarget(name: "llama", url: ".../releases/download/b11493/llama-b11493-xcframework.zip", checksum: …)` — **zero compile time**.
- Wrappers: [`mattt/llama.swift`](https://github.com/mattt/llama.swift) (SPM, re-exports C API, tracks upstream as `2.<build>.0`, iOS 16+); [`eastriverlee/LLM.swift`](https://github.com/eastriverlee/LLM.swift) (MIT, iOS 16+, pins b10068 xcframework, uses GGUF-embedded chat template, `LLM(from: Bundle.main.url(forResource:"m", withExtension:"gguf")!, template: .chatML(sys))` then `respond(to:)`; `@Generatable` structured output); `ShenghaiWang/SwiftLlama` (older).
- **Simulator: runs CPU-only** (simulator slice exists; "Simulator does not support Metal compute"). Metal shaders JIT on first load (~1–2 s, cached).
- Bundle GGUF as a real uncompressed file (mmap). Raw C API: `llama_model_default_params()` → `n_gpu_layers = 99`; `llama_model_load_from_file`; `llama_init_from_model` with `n_ctx`, `n_batch`, `flash_attn_type`, `type_k/type_v = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0` (halves KV); template: `llama_model_chat_template(model, nil)` + `llama_chat_apply_template(tmpl, msgs, n, true, buf, len)`.
- **Guaranteed JSON**: `llama_sampler_init_grammar(vocab, gbnf, "root")` in the sampler chain. The JSON-schema→GBNF converter is C++ `common/`, not in the xcframework — hand-write ~5 GBNF rules (`root ::= "{" ws "\"summary\":" ws string "," ws "\"decisions\":" ws arr "," ws "\"action_items\":" ws arr "}"`) or pre-generate with `json_schema_to_grammar.py`.
- Speed: llama.cpp Q4_K_M 1B ≈ **40–50 tok/s on 16 Pro, 35–45 on 15 Pro**, ~800 MB RSS ([ertas, Apr 2026](https://www.ertas.ai/blog/llm-run-on-iphone-benchmarks)); same model on 17 Pro Gemma-4-E2B: llama.cpp 38.8 vs MLX 49.1 tok/s (MLX ~25% faster decode; llama.cpp far lower RSS).

## 3. Other routes (2026)

- **LiteRT-LM** (replaces MediaPipe LLM Inference, now "maintenance-only"): Swift API is **"Early Preview"**; Gemma-4-E2B on 17 Pro: 56–61 tok/s, 532–3,513 tok/s prefill, 497 MB RSS — but model is 2.58 GB and it's Gemma-centric. Skip.
- **Apple "Core AI"** (iOS 27, successor to Core ML): BYO open LLM via `coreai-torch` → `.aimodel`; Qwen3-0.6B 193 tok/s on 17 Pro; ANE keeps 67% under sustained load vs MLX 38%. Needs iOS 27 + conversion pipeline → not for 6 h. Classic Core ML (john-rocky/CoreML-LLM): Qwen3.5-2B 27 tok/s on ANE; conversion-heavy.
- **ExecuTorch**: experimental Swift `TextLLMRunner` (Llama/Qwen3/Phi-4-mini `.pte`), needs export; no fresh iPhone numbers. **mlc-llm**: compile-per-model; not re-verified.
- **Licensing traps**: Liquid **LEAP SDK** is free, but LFM2/LFM2.5 weights are **LFM Open License v1.0** (free <$10M revenue; not OSI). **picoLLM** requires a Picovoice AccessKey (online validation) → not open source. Gemma 3 (Terms of Use) and Llama 3.2 (Community License) are "open-weight", not OSI. **Gemma 4 moved to Apache 2.0 (2026-04-02)**; all Qwen3/3.5 and SmolLM are Apache 2.0.

## 5. Prompting & long transcripts

- **Single pass, 8k ctx**: 1k–6k tokens fits every candidate. Prefill on 17 Pro ≈ 1–3k tok/s (2–6 s for 6k); ~2–3× slower on 15 Pro. KV budget: Qwen3-1.7B 8k ≈ 0.9 GB fp16 (set `kvBits: 8` / `type_k=q8_0`), LFM2.5/Qwen3.5 ≈ 0.1 GB. Only map-reduce if >8k tokens or 6 GB phones: chunk ~2k tokens on speaker turns, 100-token overlap, extract per chunk, one merge pass that dedupes decisions/actions.
- Pre-clean the transcript (drop timestamps, fillers) — 20–40% fewer tokens, free speed.
- **Markdown with fixed headings** (`## Summary`, `## Decisions`, `## Action Items` as `- [Owner] task — due`) is the most reliable free-form format for 1–2B models; JSON only when grammar-enforced (llama.cpp GBNF, or `MLXGuidedGeneration` JSON-Schema/EBNF — `GrammarConstraint(tokenizer:jsonSchema:…)` + `GuidedGenerationLoop.run`, iOS 17+, pre-warm off the main actor since grammar compile blocks hundreds of ms). Otherwise lenient-parse + one retry.
- System prompt <150 tokens: "Use only facts in the transcript; write 'None' if no decisions; max 5 bullets per section." Skip few-shot (prefill cost > gain). temperature 0.2–0.4, top_p 0.9, repetition_penalty 1.05–1.1, maxTokens 600–800, thinking disabled.

## Recommendation (6-hour build)

1. **MLX Swift (`mlx-swift-lm` 3.32.3) + `mlx-community/Qwen3-1.7B-4bit`** (985 MB, Apache-2.0, `enable_thinking:false`, `kvBits: 8`). Best-documented iOS path, ~40 tok/s on 17 Pro / ~30 on 15–16 Pro, ChatSession streaming in 15 lines, strict open-source. If the license bar is "open-weight", swap the folder for **`LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-MLX-4bit`** (659 MB, 60 tok/s, best IFEval) — zero code change. Try **Qwen3.5-2B text-only (1.06 GB)** last, only if time remains (long-context win, but unbenchmarked on iPhone MLX and a third-party conversion).
2. **Fallback: llama.cpp `b11493` xcframework (or LLM.swift) + Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M (1.11 GB) / LFM2.5 Q4_K_M (731 MB) + GBNF for guaranteed JSON.** No compile time, runs in the simulator (CPU), lowest RSS, ~20–25% slower decode than MLX.

Gotchas to say out loud: device-only testing for MLX; add the memory entitlement; bundle as folder reference (not compressed asset); strip `<think>`; warm up once before timing; expect thermal decay after ~2 min.

## Verdict up front

**Pick: FluidAudio + Parakeet TDT (v3 default; v2 if English-only; Redux if size-constrained and iOS 18 is OK).** Best WER per MB, ANE-only (low memory), token timings → bundled `buildWordTimings()`, documented offline folder loading, and the *same package ships speaker diarization* (`DiarizerManager`), which removes a second dependency for your merge step.

## 1. WhisperKit → `argmax-oss-swift`

- **Package**: `https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift.git` (old `argmaxinc/WhisperKit` URL redirects). Renamed at v1.0.0 (2026-05-01); **latest v1.1.0 (2026-08-06)**. Product name is still `WhisperKit`. README still says `from: "0.9.0"`; pin `from: "1.1.0"`. [releases](https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift/releases), [registry](https://swiftpackageregistry.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift)
- **Min OS**: iOS 16 / macOS 13 for WhisperKit+SpeakerKit (TTSKit needs iOS 18). Swift 6 concurrency.
- **Bundling**: `WhisperKitConfig(modelFolder: String?, ..., download: Bool = true)` and a convenience `WhisperKit(model:modelFolder:prewarm:load:download:)` exist in source ([Configurations.swift](https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift/blob/main/Sources/WhisperKit/Core/Configurations.swift), [WhisperKit.swift](https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift/blob/main/Sources/WhisperKit/Core/WhisperKit.swift)). Drag the `openai_whisper-*` folder from HF into Xcode as a **folder reference** (keeps the `.mlmodelc` dir layout), then `download: false`.
- **Timestamps**: `DecodingOptions(wordTimestamps: true)` → `TranscriptionSegment{start,end,text,words:[WordTiming]?}`, `WordTiming{word,tokens,start,end,probability}`, plus `result.allWords` ([Models.swift](https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift/blob/main/Sources/WhisperKit/Core/Models.swift)). Gotcha: words come from the decoder's `alignment_heads_weights` output; `supportsWordTimestamps` is false and words are **silently nil** if a model lacks it (all official `argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml` variants have it) ([TextDecoder.swift](https://github.com/argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift/blob/main/Sources/WhisperKit/Core/TextDecoder.swift)).
- **Sizes on disk** (summed from HF tree API, `argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml`): tiny 76 MB (tiny.en 66), base 146 MB (base.en 145), small 484 MB, `small_216MB`, `large-v3-v20240930_626MB` (= OpenAI large-v3-turbo, 809M params, quantized; the fp16 `_turbo` folder is 1.63 GB), `large-v3-v20240930_turbo_632MB`, `distil-large-v3_turbo_600MB`. Note Argmax's `_turbo` suffix means *their GPU-optimized compile*, not OpenAI's turbo. [tree](https://huggingface.co/argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml/tree/main)
- **WER (LibriSpeech, Argmax)**: 626MB 1.95; distil-large-v3 2.47; small.en 3.12; base.en 3.98; tiny.en 5.61 ([README](https://huggingface.co/argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml/raw/20f51f218879660aa966596dfe336a762249abe8/README.md)).
- **iPhone speed (Argmax dashboard, iOS 26, speed factor = audio-sec/sec)**: iPhone 16 Pro: `large-v3-v20240930_turbo_632MB` 7.6x, `distil-large-v3_turbo_600MB` 12.2x, small.en 17.2x. iPhone 15: base 44x, tiny.en 75x, turbo_632MB 5.8x. iPhone 14: base.en 40x ([performance_data.json](https://huggingface.co/spaces/argmaxinc/whisperkit-benchmarks/raw/main/dashboard_data/performance_data.json)).
- **First load**: "15–90 seconds because CoreML compiles the models on-device"; cache evicted after OS update, low disk, ~14 days idle ([Argmax docs](https://app.argmaxinc.com/docs/guides/managing-models)). `prewarm: true` compiles sequentially (lower peak RAM, slower).
- No official iPhone peak-RAM numbers; budget ≥ weights size + decoder KV.

```swift
import WhisperKit
let folder = Bundle.main.resourceURL!.appendingPathComponent("openai_whisper-base.en").path
let pipe = try await WhisperKit(WhisperKitConfig(modelFolder: folder, download: false))
let opts = DecodingOptions(language: "en", wordTimestamps: true, chunkingStrategy: .vad)
let results = try await pipe.transcribe(audioArray: samples16kMono, decodeOptions: opts)
for s in results.flatMap(\.segments) { print(s.start, s.end, s.text); s.words?.forEach { print($0.word, $0.start, $0.end, $0.probability) } }
```

## 2. FluidAudio (Parakeet TDT CoreML)

- **Package**: `https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio.git`. **Latest v0.17.7 (2026-10-08)**; README still says `from: "0.12.4"`; swiftpackageregistry is stale at 0.15.6 ([releases](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/releases)). Package.swift: **iOS 17+**, macOS 14+, visionOS 2+, swift-tools 6.0, no external deps ([Package.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Package.swift)).
- **Models** (`AsrModelVersion`): `.v2` (EN, LibriSpeech test-clean WER 2.1%), `.v3` (25 EU langs, 2.27–2.5%, "~480 MB"), `.ultra` (2.13%, int8 encoder 595 MB, iOS 17+, total ≈ 632 MB per HF tree), `.redux` (2-bit encoder 183 MB, **~220 MB download**, 2.71% WER, **iOS 18+**), `.phonon2` (fastest v3-family on ANE, 2.47%, iOS 18+) ([v0.17.3 notes](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/releases), [benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). v3 files: `Encoder.mlmodelc` 445 MB + Decoder 24 + JointDecision 13 + Preprocessor 0.5 + `parakeet_vocab.json` ≈ 483 MB (HF tree API, `FluidInference/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml`).
- **Speed**: 155–210x RTFx on M4 Pro; **no published iPhone RTFx**. iPhone 16 Pro Max encoder compile: 3.36 s cold / 0.16 s warm; iPhone 13: 4.40 s cold ([benchmarks](https://docs.fluidinference.com/reference/benchmarks.md)). RN wrapper README: ~500 MB total, first init 20–30 s, later ~1 s ([react-native-fluidaudio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/react-native-fluidaudio/main/README.md)). Independent 3rd-party estimate ~47x on iPhone 15 Pro (extrapolated, not measured) ([TowardsAI](https://pub.towardsai.net/parakeet-vs-whisper-for-local-dictation-speed-accuracy-and-vocabulary-in-2026-f809fcc4271c)).
- **Timestamps**: `ASRResult{text, confidence, duration, processingTime, tokenTimings:[TokenTiming]?}`; `TokenTiming{token, tokenId, startTime, endTime, confidence}` are **subword tokens**; free function `public func buildWordTimings(from:) -> [WordTiming{word,startTime,endTime}]` merges on `▁` boundaries ([AsrTypes.swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Sources/FluidAudio/ASR/Parakeet/AsrTypes.swift)).
- **Offline bundling**: `AsrModels.load(from: dir, configuration: AsrModels.defaultConfiguration(), version: .v3)` with the 4 `.mlmodelc` + vocab in one folder; `AsrModels.modelsExist(at:)` ([ManualModelLoading.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/main/Documentation/ASR/ManualModelLoading.md)).
- **Gotchas**: input must be 16 kHz mono Float32 — pass a file URL or use their `AudioConverter`, hand-parsed WAV gives empty output; API name churned (`initialize(models:)` → `configure` → `loadModels`) — copy from the README of the tag you pin; ANE-only, MPSGraph/BNNS crashes reported on iOS 26/27 betas (issues #844/#889); Parakeet is non-streaming batch (fine for a notetaker).
- **Bonus**: `DiarizerManager` / Nemotron-3 diarization in the same package.

```swift
import FluidAudio
let dir = Bundle.main.resourceURL!.appendingPathComponent("parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml")
let models = try await AsrModels.load(from: dir, configuration: AsrModels.defaultConfiguration(), version: .v3)
let asr = AsrManager(config: .default); try await asr.loadModels(models)
let r = try await asr.transcribe(samples16kMono, source: .system)   // or transcribe(fileURL, source: .system)
let words = buildWordTimings(from: r.tokenTimings ?? [])             // [WordTiming(word,startTime,endTime)]
```

## 3. sherpa-onnx

- Upstream **v1.13.8 (2026-09-10)**; tagged release has **no iOS asset** (build with `build-ios.sh`). Use the SPM mirror **`https://github.com/willwade/sherpa-onnx-spm.git` 1.13.8 (2026-09-14)**: `sherpa-onnx.xcframework.zip` 29.5 MB + `onnxruntime.xcframework.zip` 65.3 MB, iOS 13+ ([API](https://api.github.com/repos/willwade/sherpa-onnx-spm/releases/latest)). `uakihir0/sherpa-onnx-spm` was archived 2026-08-03.

Models: Whisper, Zipformer, Parakeet TDT v2/v3, SenseVoice, Moonshine, Dolphin, Paraformer.

## 4. whisper.cpp

- **v1.9.5 (2026-10-06)**: tagged releases ship **source only**; only nightly builds attach `whisper-bNNNN-xcframework.zip` (b5454, 62.8 MB) ([releases API](https://api.github.com/repos/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/releases?per_page=30)). SPM = `binaryTarget(url: ...xcframework.zip, checksum:)`.

- Verdict: most glue, no ANE decoder, worse WER/size than Parakeet. Skip for 6 h.

## 5. Newer options (2026)

- **Moonshine Voice** (2026-02-13, MIT): `https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine-swift`, iOS 14+, CPU-only; tiny 26 MB … medium-streaming 245 MB at **6.65% OpenASR WER** (Whisper large-v3: 7.44%), iPhone 12 latency 25–90 ms ([blog](https://petewarden.com/2026/02/13/announcing-moonshine-voice/), [iOS guide](https://mintlify.wiki/moonshine-ai/moonshine/platforms/ios)). 3. sherpa-onnx (only for exotic models), 4. Moonshine (size/speed demo, no words), 5. whisper.cpp (skip).

You are designing the concrete implementation plan for a 6-hour iOS take-home. You are READ-ONLY: do not create or edit files. You may use WebSearch/WebFetch (load via ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch") to VERIFY exact API names at the pinned versions — this is your most valuable job: wrong API names cost the builder 20 minutes each.

## The app ("Minutes")
Native SwiftUI iOS app (iOS 17+), fully offline AI meeting notetaker: record or import audio → on-device transcription with word timestamps → speaker diarization (consistent Speaker 1/2) → merge → on-device LLM writes notes (summary, key decisions, action items). English only. Test device: iPhone 15 Pro/16/17 class (8 GB RAM). Xcode 26.6. Project generated with `xcodegen` from `project.yml`. Models are downloaded ONCE on first launch into Application Support (not bundled), then everything is offline. No cloud, no Apple Intelligence, no Apple FoundationModels, no SpeechAnalyzer.

## Stack already decided (do not re-litigate; verify and detail)
1. **FluidAudio** SPM `https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio.git` pinned `from: "0.17.7"` (iOS 17+, swift-tools 6.0).
   - ASR: Parakeet TDT 0.6B `.v2` (English). Known API surface from research: `AsrModels.downloadAndLoad(version:)` / `AsrModels.load(from:configuration:version:)`, `AsrManager(config: .default)`, `asr.loadModels(models)`, `asr.transcribe(samples, source: .system)` → `ASRResult{text, tokenTimings:[TokenTiming]?}`, free func `buildWordTimings(from:) -> [WordTiming{word,startTime,endTime}]`, `AudioConverter().resampleAudioFile(url)` → 16 kHz mono Float32. API names churned across versions — VERIFY against the v0.17.7 tag (README + Sources/FluidAudio/ASR/*.swift + Documentation/ASR/*.md).
   - Diarization: `OfflineDiarizerManager(config:)` with `OfflineDiarizerConfig.default`, `cfg.clustering.numSpeakers / maxSpeakers`, `prepareModels()` (auto-download) or `prepareModels(directory:)`, `process(audio: samples)` / `process(url)` → `DiarizationResult{segments:[TimedSpeakerSegment{speakerId,startTimeSeconds,endTimeSeconds}]}`. VERIFY exact names at v0.17.7 (Sources/FluidAudio/Diarizer/Offline/*.swift, Documentation/Diarization/*.md, docs.fluidinference.com/diarization/offline-pipeline). Also verify where FluidAudio stores downloaded models (Application Support/FluidAudio/Models?) and how to set a custom directory / check `modelsExist`.
2. **LLM.swift** `https://github.com/eastriverlee/LLM.swift` (MIT, iOS 16+, wraps a pinned llama.cpp xcframework via binaryTarget). VERIFY at latest tag: init signature (`LLM(from: URL, template: Template, maxTokenCount:...)`), `Template.chatML(systemPrompt)` or GGUF-embedded template, streaming (`respond(to:)` with `update` closure / AsyncStream), stop sequences, sampling params (temperature/topP/repeat penalty), whether a grammar/`@Generatable` structured output exists and how it works, how it handles `n_ctx`, and memory/threads defaults. Model: `Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M.gguf` — find the exact direct download URL (prefer `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF` official repo, else `unsloth/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF`) and file size. Note Qwen3 thinking: `/no_think` soft switch and stripping `<think>…</think>`.
3. **Merge**: port of whisperX `assign_word_speakers`: per word pick max-overlap diarization segment, else nearest by midpoint; fold into turns; merge same-speaker turns with gap < 0.75 s; reassign 1–2-word islands. Pure function + one assert-based test.
4. Audio: `AVAudioEngine` input tap → `AVAudioConverter` → 16 kHz mono Float32 WAV via `AVAudioFile`; import via `.fileImporter(allowedContentTypes: [.audio])` with security-scoped access → decode any format to 16 kHz Float32 (`AVAudioFile` + `AVAudioConverter`). Playback `AVAudioPlayer`. Background audio mode for long recordings.
5. Persistence: JSON file per meeting + WAV in Application Support/Meetings/<id>/. Export Markdown via ShareLink.
6. Design: SwiftUI, custom Theme (tokens already specified elsewhere); screens: Home (list + Record + Import), Record (timer + waveform), Setup (first-run model downloads with progress), Meeting (Notes | Transcript segmented; speaker rename; tap-to-seek), stage stepper while processing.

## Deliver (dense, concrete, ≤ 2000 words):
A. **Verified API cheat-sheet** for FluidAudio 0.17.7 (ASR v2 + offline diarizer + AudioConverter + model dirs) and LLM.swift (latest tag) — exact Swift snippets that compile, with the file/URL you verified each against. Flag anything you could not verify.
B. **`project.yml`** (XcodeGen) complete draft: iOS 17.0 target "Minutes", bundle id placeholder, SPM packages (FluidAudio, LLM.swift), Info.plist keys (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, UIBackgroundModes audio, UIFileSharingEnabled?, LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace?), entitlements (increased-memory-limit), Swift 5 language mode (avoid strict-concurrency fights), ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING off if needed, a unit-test target.
C. **ModelManager design**: unified first-run flow — FluidAudio's own downloaders for ASR+diarizer (how to observe progress? if no progress API, what to show), `URLSessionDownloadTask` with progress + resume for the GGUF; readiness check; total sizes shown to the user; where files live.
D. **Pipeline design**: stage enum, sequential stages (Transcribing → Identifying speakers → Writing notes), timing capture per stage, cancellation, main-actor publishing; memory: when to load/unload ASR vs LLM on an 8 GB phone.
E. **Notes generation**: system prompt (<150 tokens) + user prompt format (speaker-labelled transcript, timestamps stripped), fixed-heading Markdown output (`## Summary`, `## Key Decisions`, `## Action Items` with `- [Owner] task`), lenient parser into `Notes{summary, decisions:[String], actionItems:[ActionItem{text, owner?, done}]}`, retry-once policy, token budget strategy for 10–30 min meetings (truncate/chunk rule), streaming display.
F. **Risk register**: top 8 things likely to break in a 6-hour build with this stack and the 1-line mitigation for each (e.g., FluidAudio API churn, ANE compile on first run, AVAudioSession category conflicts with recording+playback, security-scoped URL import, free-team entitlement failure, GGUF download interruption, Qwen3 think tags, thermal throttling).
G. **Ordered build steps** mapped to this timeline: 0:00–0:20 scaffold; 0:20–0:55 audio; 0:55–2:00 ML pipeline; 2:00–2:45 LLM; 2:45–4:15 UI; 4:15–5:00 tuning; 5:00–5:45 write-up. Each step: files touched, "done when" check.

Be precise; prefer verified facts over assumptions; mark unverified items clearly.

  All verification is done; the working directory is empty so there is nothing local to reuse. Final plan follows.
  
  ## A. Verified API cheat-sheet
  
  **FluidAudio v0.17.7** (tag exists, cut 2026-10-08; `Package.swift`: swift-tools 6.0, iOS 17+, pulls `NemoTextProcessing` binary + 2 C++ wrappers). Verified by grepping raw sources at the tag; file paths given.
  
  **Key finding:** the README/`Documentation/ASR/GettingStarted.md` snippets `transcribe(samples)` / `transcribe(samples, source: .system)` are **stale — they do not compile at 0.17.7**. All public batch overloads take `decoderState: inout TdtDecoderState` (`Sources/FluidAudio/ASR/Parakeet/SlidingWindow/TDT/AsrManager.swift` lines 376/400/501; the CLI's `TranscribeCommand.swift` line 617 uses exactly this).
  
  ```swift
  import FluidAudio
  // First run (downloads to Application Support/FluidAudio/Models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-coreml, ~443 MB)
  let models = try await AsrModels.downloadAndLoad(version: .v2) { p in   // ProgressHandler = @Sendable (DownloadProgress) -> Void
      // p.fractionCompleted: Double; p.phase: .listing | .downloading(completedFiles:totalFiles:) | .compiling(modelName:)
  }
  // Later runs (no network): AsrModels.loadFromCache(version: .v2)
  // Readiness: AsrModels.modelsExist(at: AsrModels.defaultCacheDirectory(for: .v2), version: .v2)
  let asr = AsrManager(config: ASRConfig(parallelChunkConcurrency: 2))   // public actor; .default = 4 workers
  try await asr.loadModels(models)
  var state = TdtDecoderState.make(decoderLayers: await asr.decoderLayerCount)   // v2 = 2 layers
  let result = try await asr.transcribe(wavURL, decoderState: &state)  // also transcribe([Float], decoderState:) / (AVAudioPCMBuffer, …)
  let words = buildWordTimings(from: result.tokenTimings ?? [])         // free func, AsrTypes.swift:183 -> [WordTiming{word,startTime,endTime}]
  await asr.cleanup()                                                     // drops MLModels
  ```
  - `ASRResult{text, confidence, duration, processingTime, tokenTimings:[TokenTiming]?, …}`; `TokenTiming{token, tokenId, startTime, endTime, confidence}` — `token` already has `▁`→space (`normalizedTimingToken`, AsrManager.swift:526), so `buildWordTimings` splits correctly on batch output.
  - Long audio: chunked internally in 15 s windows (`ASRConstants.maxModelSamples = 240_000`); URL input streams from disk (`streamingEnabled` default true). No own chunking.
  - Progress: `await asr.transcriptionProgressStream` (`AsyncThrowingStream<Double,Error>`), emitted only when audio > 15 s. **Unverified semantics:** subscribe in a `Task` *before* calling `transcribe` (session is created lazily via `ensureSession()`).
  
  ```swift
  // Diarizer — Diarizer/Offline/Core/OfflineDiarizerManager.swift, OfflineDiarizerTypes.swift, OfflineDiarizerModels.swift
  var cfg = OfflineDiarizerConfig.default            // `public static var default`; OfflineDiarizerConfig() also valid
  cfg.clustering.minSpeakers = 1; cfg.clustering.maxSpeakers = 4   // Int?; also numSpeakers: Int?, threshold: 0.6
  let dm = try await OfflineDiarizerModels.load(progressHandler: { p in … })  // auto-downloads via ModelHub (.diarizer, variant "offline"), ~22 MB
  let dia = OfflineDiarizerManager(config: cfg)      // final class
  dia.initialize(models: dm)                          // alt: try await dia.prepareModels(directory:configuration:forceRedownload:) — no progress
  let r = try await dia.process(wavURL) { done, total in … }   // or process(audio: [Float], progressCallback:)

Synchronous llama_model_load_from_file — never call on main.
bot.systemPrompt = SYSTEM                  // used when template == nil → embedded GGUF jinja (llm_chat_render)
bot.temp = 0.7; bot.topP = 0.8; bot.topK = 20; bot.repeatPenalty = 1.05
bot.update = { delta in Task { @MainActor in if let d = delta { partial += d } } }   // delta callback runs off-main
bot.reset()                                 // clears history + KV cache
await bot.respond(to: userPrompt, thinking: .suppressed)   // ThinkingMode: .none | .suppressed | .enabled
let text = bot.output                       // @Published, set via @MainActor setOutput

```

- GGUF: official `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF` has **only Q8_0 (1.83 GB)**. Use `https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M.gguf` — **1,107,409,472 bytes**, 302→CDN, `accept-ranges: bytes`. Qwen3 non-thinking sampling: temp 0.7 / topP 0.8 / topK 20; `/no_think` soft switch; 32k context.

**Unverified:** progress-stream subscribe timing; Qwen3 jinja rendering under llama b10068 (auto-fallback exists); first-run ANE compile duration; `UIFileSharingEnabled` only for dev convenience.

## B. `project.yml`

```yaml
name: Minutes
options: { bundleIdPrefix: com.example, deploymentTarget: { iOS: "17.0" }, xcodeVersion: "26.6", createIntermediateGroups: true }
packages:
  FluidAudio: { url: https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio.git, exactVersion: 0.17.7 }
  LLM:        { url: https://github.com/eastriverlee/LLM.swift, exactVersion: 3.0.3 }
settings:
  base: { SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0", SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY: minimal, ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: "NO", CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic, DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: XXXXXXXXXX }
targets:
  Minutes:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    sources: [Minutes]
    dependencies:
      - { package: FluidAudio, product: FluidAudio }
      - { package: LLM, product: LLM }
    info:
      path: Minutes/Info.plist
      properties:
        CFBundleDisplayName: Minutes
        NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Minutes records meetings and processes them entirely on this device.
        UIBackgroundModes: [audio]
        UIFileSharingEnabled: true            # dev convenience: pull WAV/JSON via Finder; drop LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace
        UILaunchScreen: {}
        UISupportedInterfaceOrientations: [UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait]
        ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false
    entitlements:
      path: Minutes/Minutes.entitlements
      properties: { com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit: true }   # delete this block if a personal team fails signing
    settings: { base: { PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.minutes, TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1" } }
  MinutesTests:
    type: bundle.unit-test
    platform: iOS
    sources: [MinutesTests]
    dependencies: [{ target: Minutes }]
```
`exactVersion` on purpose: FluidAudio ships breaking renames between patch tags.

## C. ModelManager

`@MainActor final class ModelManager: ObservableObject` with `@Published var progress: [Component: Double]` and `@Published var phase: [Component: String]`; `enum Component { asr(443 MB), diarizer(22 MB), llm(1.03 GiB) }` — Setup shows three rows plus "≈1.5 GB total, Wi-Fi recommended".

- **ASR/diarizer:** FluidAudio's own downloaders; progress from `DownloadProgress.fractionCompleted`; phase copy: `.downloading(c,t)` → "Downloading c/t", `.compiling` → "Optimizing for your device…" (this is where first-run ANE compile blocks; do it here, not in the pipeline). Drop the returned `AsrModels` after setup.
- **GGUF:** `URLSession(configuration: .default, delegate: self, delegateQueue: nil)`; `downloadTask(with:)`; `didWriteData` → progress; `didFinishDownloadingTo` → `moveItem` to `AppSupport/Models/Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M.gguf`; on error read `userInfo[NSURLSessionDownloadTaskResumeData]`, write to `AppSupport/Models/qwen.resume`, next attempt `downloadTask(withResumeData:)`; if that errors immediately (expired signed CDN URL) delete the resume blob and restart. Sanity: final size ≥ 1.0 GB else delete. Foreground session only (background session needs AppDelegate plumbing — skipped).
- Run all three with `async let`; on success `ModelHub.offlineMode = true`, `UserDefaults modelsReady = true`, mark `AppSupport/FluidAudio` and `AppSupport/Models` `isExcludedFromBackup`.
- `isReady`: `AsrModels.modelsExist(at: AsrModels.defaultCacheDirectory(for: .v2), version: .v2)` && the 5 diarizer files exist under `OfflineDiarizerModels.defaultModelsDirectory()/speaker-diarization-coreml` && GGUF exists. Root gate: `isReady ? HomeView : SetupView`.
- Layout: `AppSupport/FluidAudio/Models/…` (library-owned), `AppSupport/Models/*.gguf`, `AppSupport/Meetings/<uuid>/{meeting.json, audio.wav}`.

## D. Pipeline

```swift
enum Stage: String { case transcribing = "Transcribing", diarizing = "Identifying speakers", writing = "Writing notes" }
struct StageTiming: Codable { let stage: String; let seconds: Double }
@MainActor final class Pipeline: ObservableObject {
  @Published var stage: Stage?; @Published var progress: Double?; @Published var partial = ""; @Published var error: String?
  private var task: Task<Void, Never>?; private var bot: LLM?
  func run(_ m: Meeting) { task = Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { … } }   // each stage: t0 = Date(); publish via MainActor.run; append StageTiming
  func cancel() { task?.cancel(); bot?.stop() }
}
```
1. **Transcribing:** `loadFromCache(.v2)` → `AsrManager(config: ASRConfig(parallelChunkConcurrency: 2))` → progress-stream Task → `transcribe(wavURL, decoderState:)` → `buildWordTimings` → `cleanup()`, nil the models. Persist transcript immediately.
2. **Identifying speakers:** `OfflineDiarizerModels.load()` → `initialize` → `process(wavURL) {done,total}` → `Merge.assign(words:segments:)` (whisperX port: max-overlap else nearest midpoint; fold to turns; merge same-speaker gap < 0.75 s; reassign 1–2-word islands) → speaker ids → "Speaker N" by first appearance; nil the manager. Persist.
3. **Writing notes:** `LLM(from:…)` inside the detached task, `reset()`, stream to `partial`, parse, persist, `bot = nil`.
- `Task.checkCancellation()` between stages; FluidAudio calls are not interruptible mid-call (accepted), LLM stops instantly.
- Memory: models never co-resident. Peaks ≈ ASR 1.2 GB / LLM 1.1 GB weights + ~0.9 GB KV at 8192 — under the default jetsam ceiling even without the entitlement. `UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true` while processing; tell the user to keep the app open (background mode only keeps *recording* alive).

## E. Notes generation

System prompt (~90 tokens):
> You write meeting notes. Reply in Markdown with exactly these sections and nothing else: `## Summary` (3–5 sentences), `## Key Decisions` (one per line as "- …", or "- None"), `## Action Items` (one per line as "- [Owner] task", Owner is a speaker name or "Unassigned"). Use only the transcript. Be concise.

User prompt: `Transcript:\n\nSpeaker 1: …\nSpeaker 2: …\n\nWrite the notes. /no_think` (timestamps stripped, turns merged).

- Budget: `maxTokenCount: 8192`; reserve 700 output + ~150 system/template → prompt ≤ 7300 tokens (≈ 5400 words; 30 min of speech ≈ 4500 words fits). Measure with `bot.encode(prompt).count`; if over, drop turns from the middle until it fits and insert `[… omitted …]`. No map-reduce chunking (YAGNI ≤ 30 min).
- Parser (lenient): strip `<think>…</think>` and ``` fences; headers match `^#{1,3}\s*|^\*\*` + `summary|key decisions|action items` case-insensitive; bullets `-`, `*`, `•`, `\d+.`; action owner regex `^\[(.+?)\]\s*(.+)$` or `^(.+?):\s(.+)$`; "None" → empty list.
- Retry once if `summary` empty (temp 0.5, append "Your previous reply did not follow the format."); if still empty, store raw text as summary so nothing is lost.
- Streaming: `partial` rendered as plain text in the Notes tab during `.writing`; replaced by styled sections on completion.
- `Notes: Codable { summary: String; decisions: [String]; actionItems: [ActionItem] }`, `ActionItem { id = UUID(); text; owner: String?; done = false }`.

## F. Risk register

1. **FluidAudio API churn** — docs show `transcribe(_:source:)`; 0.17.7 only has `transcribe(_:decoderState:language:)`. Use `TdtDecoderState.make(decoderLayers:)`; pin `exactVersion`.
2. **SPM resolve/build time** — swift-syntax macro build + swift-testing clone + 100 MB llama xcframework + NemoTextProcessing binary ≈ 5–10 min. Run `xcodegen generate` + resolve at minute 0; never Clean Build Folder.
3. **First-run ANE compile** of the 425 MB encoder (30–120 s, inside `AsrModels.load`) — do it in Setup with "Optimizing…" copy; cached by CoreML afterwards.
4. **AVAudioSession conflicts** — one category app-wide at launch: `.playAndRecord`, `.default`, `[.defaultToSpeaker, .allowBluetooth]`; activate before `engine.start()`; on `interruptionNotification` stop and finalize the file (written incrementally, so nothing is lost).
5. **Security-scoped import** — `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()`, copy into the sandbox *first*, `stop`, then decode the copy with `AudioConverter`.
6. **Entitlement on a personal team** — `increased-memory-limit` breaks automatic signing; remove the key; design already fits without it.
7. **GGUF download interruption** — resume data can be rejected once the signed CDN URL expires → discard and restart; show MB/total; size sanity check.
8. **Qwen3 think tags / thermal** — `.none` enables thinking: use `.suppressed` + `/no_think` + parser strip; check `ProcessInfo.thermalState`, drop `parallelChunkConcurrency` to 1 when `.serious`; disable Low Power Mode for the demo (halves Metal throughput).

| 2:45–4:15 UI | `HomeView`, `RecordView` (timer + bars), `SetupView`, `MeetingView` (Notes/Transcript segmented, `ProcessingStepper`, rename sheet, tap-word → seek), `ShareLink(item: meeting.markdown)` | Full record → process → notes → export works untethered |

| 5:00–5:45 write-up | `README.md` | Architecture, model choices, timing table from `StageTiming`, limits |

# Plan: "Minutes" — offline AI meeting notetaker (iOS, 6 h)

## Context
Founder take-home: an iOS app that records or imports a meeting and, fully on-device, transcribes it with timestamps, labels Speaker 1 and Speaker 2 consistently, and writes notes (summary, decisions, action items). It is judged on accuracy, design, UX, app size, performance and how well the coding agent is driven. Cloud AI, Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models are not allowed. Product reference: **Granola** (a blank notepad while you listen; AI then *enhances your notes* with the transcript; clean, editorial look).

## Stack (3 pieces, no custom ML)
| Job | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Speech-to-text | **iOS 26 `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber`** (Speech framework, on-device; not Apple Intelligence). Uses `attributeOptions: [.audioTimeRange]` for word timestamps, and `AssetInventory` installs the English model once. | Streams live while you record, so the transcript is ready the moment you stop. The model is OS-managed, so it adds **0 MB** to the app. Benchmarks put it at ~2 % WER, ahead of on-device Whisper. |
| Speaker diarization | **FluidAudio `OfflineDiarizerManager`** (SPM, `exactVersion: 0.17.7`), with `clustering.maxSpeakers = 2` by default | pyannote community-1 with VBx global clustering gives consistent IDs across the whole file. ~22 MB of models, runs on the ANE, ~15 % DER. |
| Notes LLM | **LLM.swift 3.0.3** (llama.cpp prebuilt, no compile step) + **Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M GGUF** (1.1 GB, Apache-2.0, from `unsloth/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF`) | Memory-mapped weights keep RAM low, and it runs at ~35–45 tok/s on a 15 Pro. Use `respond(to:thinking: .suppressed)` and strip any `<think>` blocks. |
| Text-to-speech | `AVSpeechSynthesizer` "Listen to notes" button | On-device, ~10 lines. |

Fallback if a reviewer objects to Apple Speech: switch the transcriber to FluidAudio Parakeet v2 (same package, one file, +450 MB).
Models download once in a first-run Setup screen; after that everything works in Airplane Mode.

## Flow
1. **Record:** an `AVAudioEngine` tap feeds SpeechAnalyzer for the live transcript and writes `audio.wav` (16 kHz mono). The screen shows a Granola-style blank notepad (`TextEditor`) for your own notes, plus a collapsible live transcript and waveform.
2. **Stop:** FluidAudio diarizes the WAV (seconds). `Merge.swift` gives each word the speaker segment it overlaps most (or the nearest one if none overlaps), groups words into turns, and merges same-speaker turns with gaps under 0.75 s.
3. **Enhance:** Qwen3 gets your notes plus the speaker-labelled transcript. It returns Markdown with `## Summary`, `## Key Decisions` and `## Action Items` (`- [Owner] task`), streamed live. A lenient parser fills `Notes`.
4. **Import** (`.fileImporter`, audio files) runs the same steps from a file.

## Files (`project.yml` via xcodegen, iOS 26 target, ~12 Swift files)
`MinutesApp`, `Theme` (tokens, press style, haptics), `Models` (Meeting/Turn/Word/Notes, Codable; one JSON + WAV per meeting in Application Support), `Recorder`, `Transcriber` (SpeechAnalyzer for live and file input), `Diarizer`, `Merge` + `MergeTests` (one assert test), `NotesWriter`, `Setup`/`ModelManager` (FluidAudio progress plus a `URLSession` GGUF download with resume), and views `Home`, `Record`, `Meeting` (Notes | Transcript tabs, tap a speaker to rename, tap a turn to seek, `ShareLink` Markdown export, Listen).

## Design (impeccable + apple-design + awesome-ios-design-md Bear/Apple Notes tokens)
- **Colour:** warm paper `#FBFAF6` (light) and charcoal `#1C1E22` (dark, never pure black); ink `#1F2126`. One accent, deep teal `#0F766E`; the only red is the record button (`#E5484D`). Speaker chips: indigo `#4F6BED` and amber `#D97A2B`.
- **Type and layout:** SF Pro with Dynamic Type, negative tracking on large titles, monospaced digits for timers. Spacing on a 4/8/16/24 grid, radius 12, hairlines instead of shadows.
- **Motion:** critically damped springs (`response 0.35`). Buttons react on press-down (scale 0.97). Haptics on record, stop and check-off. Respect Reduce Motion.
- **Banned:** gradients, cards inside cards, bare spinners. Processing shows a 3-step stepper with elapsed times.

## Timeline
| Time | Work |
|---|---|
| Before the clock | Install Xcode 26.6, `brew install xcodegen`, enable Developer Mode on the iPhone, `git init`. |
| 0:00–0:30 | Scaffold, theme and models; the app runs on the phone. |
| 0:30–1:30 | Recorder and live SpeechAnalyzer transcript; file import. |
| 1:30–2:30 | Setup screen downloads, diarizer, merge and its test. |
| 2:30–3:15 | NotesWriter (prompt, streaming, parser). |
| 3:15–4:45 | UI polish across all screens, dark mode, empty and error states, TTS. |
| 4:45–5:15 | Tune on 2 real clips; log per-stage timings and peak memory. |
| 5:15–6:00 | README (models, sizes, timings, trade-offs, limits), AI-workflow reflection, session export (claude-devtools), demo video in Airplane Mode. |

## Verification
- `MergeTests` passes.
- On a real iPhone in Airplane Mode: record a 2-minute two-person chat, stop, and check that you get correct Speaker 1/2 turns and parsed notes.
- Import a 10-minute file: diarization plus notes should finish in under 60 s, with peak memory under 2.5 GB in the Xcode gauge.
- Check dark mode and Dynamic Type XL.

Judged on accuracy, design, UX, app size, inference performance, and *how well the coding agent was driven*. Deliverables: repo, offline demo video, technical summary, agent session history, AI-workflow reflection.

-Hard constraints: no cloud AI, no Apple Intelligence, no Apple Foundation Models framework. (We also avoid iOS 26 `SpeechAnalyzer` — it's Apple's on-device speech stack and a reviewer could reasonably count it under "Apple Intelligence"; open-source models are what the brief asks to see judged.)

-Goal of this plan: the laziest stack that is *actually good* — three mature Swift packages, one XcodeGen project, ~15 Swift files, zero custom ML code — so the 6 hours go to accuracy tuning, UX polish, and the write-up.
-| Xcode | Not installed on this Mac → install **Xcode 26.6** (stable; needs macOS ≥ 26.2, you have 26.6.2) **before the 6h clock starts**. No Xcode 27 betas. |

DER **15.1 % @122× RTFx** default, 13.9 % @65× max-accuracy (VoxConverse, M2); AMI-SDM 12.0 %. Runs on ANE. `clustering.numSpeakers = 2` + `maxSpeakers = 2` (fixed in PR #802 → must be ≥ 0.15.6). -| ASR | **FluidAudio Parakeet TDT 0.6B `.v2`** (English-only — your choice; same package as diarizer) | LibriSpeech WER **2.1 %** (vs whisper base.en 3.98 %, small.en 3.12 %, large-v3-turbo 1.95 %). ~**480 MB** CoreML (Encoder 445 + Decoder 24 + Joint 13 + vocab), ANE-only → low RAM, fast (155–210× RTFx on M4 Pro; iPhone unpublished, est. ≥30×; encoder compile 3.4 s cold / 0.16 s warm on 16 Pro Max). Token timings → `buildWordTimings(from:)` gives word-level `[WordTiming]`. Size alternative in one enum flip: `.redux` (2-bit encoder, **~220 MB**, 2.71 % WER, iOS 18+). +## Design (impeccable + apple-design + awesome-ios-design-md Bear/Apple Notes tokens)

-  - `accent` #0F766E deep teal (primary actions, progress, links; pressed #0B5F58) · `record` #E5484D is the **only** red; `success` #34C759 · `warning` #F2C14E

-  - Speakers (equal lightness so neither dominates, works on both schemes): S1 `#4F6BED` indigo · S2 `#D97A2B` amber · S3 `#2F9E7E` green · S4 `#B5508F` plum. Color is never the only cue — the name label is always rendered.

-- **Spacing/shape:** 4-pt grid, only 4/8/12/16/24/32; screen gutter 16; row min-height 44; radius 10 (fields) / 12 (buttons, surfaces) / capsule (speaker chips); hairlines instead of shadows; toolbars on `.regularMaterial` (depth = material, not decoration).

-- **Motion (apple-design → SwiftUI):** default UI `.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 1.0)` (critically damped, interruptible by default in SwiftUI); sheets/flicks `.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8)`; feedback on press-*down* via a `ButtonStyle` scaling to 0.97 on `isPressed`; symmetric enter/exit transitions, anchored origins; only animate transform/opacity (never layout-shifting props — Bear rule); recording waveform = `TimelineView` + `Canvas` of RMS bars; progress is determinate when known else a soft pulsing dot — never a bare spinner; honor `accessibilityReduceMotion` (drop scale/pulse, keep opacity).

-- **Perf rules carried over from the RN skill:** virtualized transcript (`List`/`LazyVStack` with stable `Identifiable` ids, never a plain `VStack` of 1 000 rows); no per-row closures allocating; images none; native navigation (`NavigationStack`) and native sheets with `presentationDetents`; safe-area-aware scrolling; `Button` with custom style, not tap gestures on views.

-- **States designed, not defaulted:** empty home (one sentence + Record + Import), first-run model setup (per-model rows with size, speed, determinate progress), processing (stage stepper: Transcribing → Identifying speakers → Writing notes, each with elapsed time, cancellable), error (plain language + Retry), notes (Summary / Decisions / Action items as checkable rows).
-- **Accessibility basics:** Dynamic Type (no fixed heights), 44-pt targets, VoiceOver labels ("Record", "Stop recording", row = "Speaker 1, 00:12, text"), AA contrast on every interactive element.
-## Verification (how we know it works, end-to-end)

-1. **Build/deploy:** `xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -scheme AINotetaker -destination 'id=<iphone udid>' build` (or ⌘R in Xcode). Real device only — MLX needs the GPU, CoreML in Simulator is CPU-only and slow.

-2. **Unit check (ponytail's one test):** `SpeakerMergeTests` — 6 hand-made words across 2 diarization segments, one word in a gap → expects 2 turns, gap word assigned to nearest, island reassigned. Runs with ⌘U; fails loudly if the merge regresses.

-3. **Pipeline smoke on device:** Import a known 2-speaker clip (self-record a 2-min conversation with a friend / use a public 2-speaker podcast snippet). Expect: transcript readable, 2 speakers, turns switch at the right places, timestamps monotonic, Notes JSON parsed. Timings logged to console *and* stored in `Meeting.timings` (shown as a chip in MeetingView — doubles as evidence for the write-up).
-4. **Offline proof:** Airplane Mode on → kill app → relaunch → record → full pipeline completes. (Models were fetched once on first run.)

-5. **Performance gates (iPhone 15 Pro-class):** 10-min meeting → transcription + diarization ≤ ~60 s combined, notes ≤ ~30 s, peak memory ≤ ~2.5 GB (Xcode Debug navigator Memory gauge), no thermal throttling across two consecutive runs. -- `README.md` = technical summary: models + versions, binary size (from Xcode Organizer / `du -sh` of .app), per-model on-disk size, measured inference times (log them in-app: transcription s, diarization s, LLM tok/s & total s for an N-minute file), memory peak (Xcode Debug Navigator screenshot), trade-offs, known limitations.

-- `docs/sessions/` = exported Claude Code transcripts (claude-devtools → Markdown), redacted.

-- Demo video: Airplane Mode visible in status bar → record 60–90 s two-person conversation → stop → watch stage stepper → scroll transcript with speakers → notes → rename speaker → share/export. Also show "Import" with a pre-recorded 10-min meeting to demonstrate speed.
+- On a real iPhone in Airplane Mode: record a 2-minute two-person chat, stop, and check that you get correct Speaker 1/2 turns and parsed notes.
+- Import a 10-minute file: diarization plus notes should finish in under 60 s, with peak memory under 2.5 GB in the Xcode gauge.

# Plan: "Minutes" — offline AI meeting notetaker (iOS, 6 h)

## Context
Founder take-home: an iOS app that records or imports a meeting and, fully on-device, transcribes it with timestamps, labels Speaker 1 and Speaker 2 consistently, and writes notes (summary, decisions, action items). It is judged on accuracy, design, UX, app size, performance and how well the coding agent is driven. Cloud AI, Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models are not allowed. Product reference: **Granola** (a blank notepad while you listen; AI then *enhances your notes* with the transcript; clean, editorial look).

## Stack (3 pieces, no custom ML)
| Job | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Speech-to-text | **iOS 26 `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber`** (Speech framework, on-device; not Apple Intelligence). Uses `attributeOptions: [.audioTimeRange]` for word timestamps, and `AssetInventory` installs the English model once. | Streams live while you record, so the transcript is ready the moment you stop. The model is OS-managed, so it adds **0 MB** to the app. Benchmarks put it at ~2 % WER, ahead of on-device Whisper. |
| Speaker diarization | **FluidAudio `OfflineDiarizerManager`** (SPM, `exactVersion: 0.17.7`), with `clustering.maxSpeakers = 2` by default | pyannote community-1 with VBx global clustering gives consistent IDs across the whole file. ~22 MB of models, runs on the ANE, ~15 % DER. |
| Notes LLM | **LLM.swift 3.0.3** (llama.cpp prebuilt, no compile step) + **Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M GGUF** (1.1 GB, Apache-2.0, from `unsloth/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF`) | Memory-mapped weights keep RAM low, and it runs at ~35–45 tok/s on a 15 Pro. Use `respond(to:thinking: .suppressed)` and strip any `<think>` blocks. |
| Text-to-speech | `AVSpeechSynthesizer` "Listen to notes" button | On-device, ~10 lines. |

Fallback if a reviewer objects to Apple Speech: switch the transcriber to FluidAudio Parakeet v2 (same package, one file, +450 MB).
Models download once in a first-run Setup screen; after that everything works in Airplane Mode.

## Flow
1. **Record:** an `AVAudioEngine` tap feeds SpeechAnalyzer for the live transcript and writes `audio.wav` (16 kHz mono). The screen shows a Granola-style blank notepad (`TextEditor`) for your own notes, plus a collapsible live transcript and waveform.
2. **Stop:** FluidAudio diarizes the WAV (seconds). `Merge.swift` gives each word the speaker segment it overlaps most (or the nearest one if none overlaps), groups words into turns, and merges same-speaker turns with gaps under 0.75 s.
3. **Enhance:** Qwen3 gets your notes plus the speaker-labelled transcript. It returns Markdown with `## Summary`, `## Key Decisions` and `## Action Items` (`- [Owner] task`), streamed live. A lenient parser fills `Notes`.
4. **Import** (`.fileImporter`, audio files) runs the same steps from a file.

## Files (`project.yml` via xcodegen, iOS 26 target, ~12 Swift files)
`MinutesApp`, `Theme` (tokens, press style, haptics), `Models` (Meeting/Turn/Word/Notes, Codable; one JSON + WAV per meeting in Application Support), `Recorder`, `Transcriber` (SpeechAnalyzer for live and file input), `Diarizer`, `Merge` + `MergeTests` (one assert test), `NotesWriter`, `Setup`/`ModelManager` (FluidAudio progress plus a `URLSession` GGUF download with resume), and views `Home`, `Record`, `Meeting` (Notes | Transcript tabs, tap a speaker to rename, tap a turn to seek, `ShareLink` Markdown export, Listen).

## Design (impeccable + apple-design + awesome-ios-design-md Bear/Apple Notes tokens)
- **Colour:** warm paper `#FBFAF6` (light) and charcoal `#1C1E22` (dark, never pure black); ink `#1F2126`. One accent, deep teal `#0F766E`; the only red is the record button (`#E5484D`). Speaker chips: indigo `#4F6BED` and amber `#D97A2B`.
- **Type and layout:** SF Pro with Dynamic Type, negative tracking on large titles, monospaced digits for timers. Spacing on a 4/8/16/24 grid, radius 12, hairlines instead of shadows.
- **Motion:** critically damped springs (`response 0.35`). Buttons react on press-down (scale 0.97). Haptics on record, stop and check-off. Respect Reduce Motion.
- **Banned:** gradients, cards inside cards, bare spinners. Processing shows a 3-step stepper with elapsed times.

## Timeline
| Time | Work |
|---|---|
| Before the clock | Install Xcode 26.6, `brew install xcodegen`, enable Developer Mode on the iPhone, `git init`. |
| 0:00–0:30 | Scaffold, theme and models; the app runs on the phone. |
| 0:30–1:30 | Recorder and live SpeechAnalyzer transcript; file import. |
| 1:30–2:30 | Setup screen downloads, diarizer, merge and its test. |
| 2:30–3:15 | NotesWriter (prompt, streaming, parser). |
| 3:15–4:45 | UI polish across all screens, dark mode, empty and error states, TTS. |
| 4:45–5:15 | Tune on 2 real clips; log per-stage timings and peak memory. |
| 5:15–6:00 | README (models, sizes, timings, trade-offs, limits), AI-workflow reflection, session export (claude-devtools), demo video in Airplane Mode. |

## Verification
- `MergeTests` passes.
- On a real iPhone in Airplane Mode: record a 2-minute two-person chat, stop, and check that you get correct Speaker 1/2 turns and parsed notes.
- Import a 10-minute file: diarization plus notes should finish in under 60 s, with peak memory under 2.5 GB in the Xcode gauge.
- Check dark mode and Dynamic Type XL.

# Minutes — offline AI meeting notes for iPhone

Record or import a meeting. Minutes transcribes it, tells **Speaker 1** from **Speaker 2**, and writes a summary, key decisions and action items — **entirely on-device**. After the one-time model download, it works in Airplane Mode.

Like Granola, Minutes gives you a blank notepad while it listens. Afterwards, the on-device LLM *enhances your notes* with the transcript instead of replacing them.

## Pipeline

```
mic ─► AVAudioEngine tap ─► convert once (16 kHz mono) ─┬─► SpeechAnalyzer (live, word timestamps)
                                                        └─► audio.wav
stop ─► FluidAudio diarizer (audio.wav) ─► Merge(words, speaker segments) ─► turns
     ─► Qwen3-1.7B via llama.cpp ─► Markdown notes (streamed) ─► parsed Notes
```

| Stage | Model / library | Runs on | Footprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speech-to-text | iOS 26 `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber` (Speech framework, on-device; **not** Apple Intelligence / Foundation Models) | ANE/CPU | **0 MB in app** — OS-managed asset |
| Speaker diarization | [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio) 0.17.7 `OfflineDiarizerManager`: pyannote **community-1** segmentation + WeSpeaker embeddings + PLDA + **VBx** clustering (CoreML) | ANE | ~22 MB |
| Notes | [LLM.swift](https://github.com/eastriverlee/LLM.swift) 3.0.3 (prebuilt llama.cpp xcframework, Metal) + **Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M** GGUF (Apache-2.0) | GPU | 1.1 GB (mmapped) |
| Read notes aloud | `AVSpeechSynthesizer` | CPU | 0 MB |

## Key decisions and trade-offs

- **Transcription runs live during recording.** SpeechAnalyzer streams, so the transcript is already done when you tap Stop. The only post-processing is diarization (seconds) and the notes. Imported files go through the same analyzer from disk.
- **Apple's on-device speech instead of Whisper or Parakeet.** It adds 0 MB to the app, and its published English WER (~2 %) beats every on-device Whisper size. The trade-off: iOS 26 only, and a reviewer could read it as "Apple AI". *Fallback, if needed:* FluidAudio Parakeet TDT v2 (2.1 % WER, ~450 MB) is already a dependency and can be swapped in one file (`Transcriber.swift`).
- **Global clustering is what makes speaker identities consistent.** The community-1 pipeline clusters every speaker embedding in the file at once (VBx), so "Speaker 1" at minute 1 is the same voice at minute 30. Streaming diarizers can't guarantee that. `maxSpeakers = 2` follows the brief.
- **Word→speaker merge** ([Merge.swift](Minutes/Merge.swift)) ports whisperX `assign_word_speakers`: each word goes to the speaker segment it overlaps most (or the nearest one if none overlaps). Islands of 1–2 words inside another speaker's turn are absorbed (diarization jitter), and monologues are split at pauses over 2 s.
- **llama.cpp over MLX.** It's a prebuilt binary (no 10-minute Metal/C++ compile), and mmapped weights keep resident memory far below MLX's. Decode is ~20 % slower, which doesn't matter for a ~500-token answer. Qwen3-1.7B has the best instruction-following of the Apache-licensed models under 1.2 GB; thinking is disabled (`.suppressed` + `/no_think`).
- **Markdown output, not JSON.** 1–2B models follow fixed headings more reliably than JSON. A lenient parser handles variations, and if the model ignores the format, its raw text becomes the summary, so nothing is lost.
- **Memory.** The stages never hold models at the same time: diarizer → released → LLM loaded → released. The LLM context is 8k tokens (~6k-token transcript budget ≈ 40 min of speech). Longer meetings keep the beginning and end ([NotesWriter.fit](Minutes/NotesWriter.swift)).
- **Models download once on first launch rather than ship in the bundle.** This keeps the binary small and separates *binary size* from *model footprint*.

## Measurements (iPhone ___, iOS 26.x) — fill in from the in-app timings

Each meeting stores per-stage timings, shown in the app footer and logged as `[Minutes] <stage>: N s`.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| App binary (IPA, thinned) | ___ MB |
| Model footprint on device | 22 MB (diarizer) + 1.1 GB (LLM) + OS speech asset |
| Transcription, 10-min meeting | live (0 s after stop); import: ___ s |
| Diarization, 10-min meeting | ___ s |
| Notes generation | ___ s (___ tok/s) |
| Peak memory (Xcode gauge) | ___ MB |

## Known limitations

- English only; iOS 26+; capped at 2 speakers (`Diarizer.swift`, one constant).
- Overlapping speech is assigned to one speaker (`exclusiveSegments`).
- The notes context is 8k tokens; meetings over ~40 min are trimmed in the middle (map-reduce would fix this).
- The LLM download restarts from zero if interrupted.
- Processing needs the app in the foreground (recording continues in the background).

## Build

Requires Xcode 26 and a real iPhone (the LLM runs on Metal).

```sh
brew install xcodegen
xcodegen generate && open Minutes.xcodeproj   # set your Team under Signing, run on device
```

Tests (⌘U): `MergeTests` (speaker assignment) and `NotesParseTests` (notes parser).

## Docs

- [AI workflow reflection](docs/ai-workflow.md)
- Agent session transcripts: `docs/sessions/`

# AI workflow reflection

Agent: Claude Code. Full transcripts are in `docs/sessions/`.

## How I broke the problem down

1. **Research before code.** Three research agents ran in parallel, one per hard choice: ASR, diarization, and the on-device LLM. Each had to return pinned versions, model sizes, measured iPhone numbers with sources, and a ranked pick. A planning agent then checked the exact API signatures at the pinned versions.
2. **Constraints first.** The brief bans cloud AI, Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models. Judging covers size, memory and speed. That ruled out MLX (long compile, high RSS) in favour of prebuilt llama.cpp, and favoured a 0-MB OS speech model plus a 22-MB diarizer.
3. **Thin wrappers, one pure function.** Every ML library sits behind a ~20-line wrapper. The only algorithm written by hand is the word→speaker merge, and it's pure and unit-tested.
4. **Verify against source, not READMEs.** I cloned the dependency repos at the pinned tags and grepped the public signatures.

## Where the agent was wrong or needed steering

- **Stale library docs.** FluidAudio's README shows `transcribe(samples, source:)`, but at 0.17.7 the only public overloads need an `inout TdtDecoderState`. That was caught by reading the source at the tag, before it cost a build cycle.
- **Regex literals.** The parser first used a bare `/regex/` literal, which doesn't compile in Swift 5 language mode (the project's setting). It was caught by compiling the parser with `swiftc` before Xcode was even installed; I switched to `#/…/#`.
- **A test that couldn't fail.** The first local check of the merge logic was compiled with `-O`, which strips `assert`, so it "passed" without testing anything. Rerun with `-Onone`.
- **A ~2 GB memory leak.** The LLM's streaming `update` closure captured the `LLM` instance strongly (`bot.stop()` inside it). That's a retain cycle that would keep the weights and KV cache alive after every meeting. Fixed with `[weak bot]`.
- **Main-thread decode.** Importing a file resampled the whole file on the main actor, which would freeze the UI on long files. Moved to a detached task.
- **Scope steering from me.** Mid-plan I redirected the agent: use Granola as the product reference, use iOS on-device speech-to-text and TTS, and keep the plan simple. The plan shrank from a five-stage design to three libraries and ~12 files.

## Prompting approach

- Gave the agent the full brief and the judging criteria, then asked for research *with citations* before any plan.
- Fixed hard constraints early (Xcode version, test device RAM, model delivery) with explicit questions instead of letting the agent guess.
- Asked for "the laziest stack that is actually good" (the ponytail skill): reuse library loaders, no custom ML code, one test per non-trivial function.
- Made the agent compile or run everything it could locally (merge and parser assertions, Speech framework type-check against the macOS 26 SDK, and the ML glue against the real packages) before touching a device.

2. **Constraints first.** The brief bans cloud AI, Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models. Judging covers size, memory and speed. That ruled out MLX (long compile, high RSS) in favour of prebuilt llama.cpp, and favoured a 0-MB OS speech model plus a 22-MB diarizer.
3. **Thin wrappers, one pure function.** Every ML library sits behind a ~20-line wrapper. The only algorithm written by hand is the word→speaker merge, and it's pure and unit-tested.
4. **Verify against source, not READMEs.** I cloned the dependency repos at the pinned tags and grepped the public signatures.

## Where the agent was wrong or needed steering

- **Stale library docs.** FluidAudio's README shows `transcribe(samples, source:)`, but at 0.17.7 the only public overloads need an `inout TdtDecoderState`. That was caught by reading the source at the tag, before it cost a build cycle.
- **Regex literals.** The parser first used a bare `/regex/` literal, which doesn't compile in Swift 5 language mode (the project's setting). It was caught by compiling the parser with `swiftc` before Xcode was even installed; I switched to `#/…/#`.
- **A test that couldn't fail.** The first local check of the merge logic was compiled with `-O`, which strips `assert`, so it "passed" without testing anything. Rerun with `-Onone`.
- **A ~2 GB memory leak.** The LLM's streaming `update` closure captured the `LLM` instance strongly (`bot.stop()` inside it). That's a retain cycle that would keep the weights and KV cache alive after every meeting. Fixed with `[weak bot]`.
- **Main-thread decode.** Importing a file resampled the whole file on the main actor, which would freeze the UI on long files. Moved to a detached task.
- **Scope steering from me.** Mid-plan I redirected the agent: use Granola as the product reference, use iOS on-device speech-to-text and TTS, and keep the plan simple. The plan shrank from a five-stage design to three libraries and ~12 files.

## Prompting approach

- Gave the agent the full brief and the judging criteria, then asked for research *with citations* before any plan.
- Fixed hard constraints early (Xcode version, test device RAM, model delivery) with explicit questions instead of letting the agent guess.
- Asked for "the laziest stack that is actually good" (the ponytail skill): reuse library loaders, no custom ML code, one test per non-trivial function.
- Made the agent compile or run everything it could locally (merge and parser assertions, Speech framework type-check against the macOS 26 SDK, and the ML glue against the real packages) before touching a device.
